content: 1. Fluctuations in plasma estrogen levels can occur, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. It is recommended to use a non-hormonal contraceptive method in such cases. 2. Ethinylestradiol can increase the levels or effects of dasatinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 3. Deferasirox may decrease the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 4. Demeclocycline can reduce the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 5. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of diazepam by decreasing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 6. Ethinylestradiol may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation, leading to increased serum concentrations of co-administered benzodiazepines. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 7. Dicloxacillin may decrease the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 8. Doxycycline may reduce the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are recommended. 9. Elafibranor may decrease the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Elafibranor, as a weak CYP3A4 inducer, may reduce systemic exposure to hormonal contraceptives. Switching to effective non-hormonal contraceptives or adding a barrier method is recommended during elafibranor treatment and for at least three weeks after the last dose. 10. Elagolix may decrease the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Monitoring CYP3A substrates during co-administration is advised, and dose adjustments may be required. 11. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of eltrombopag by inhibiting hepatic CYP1A2 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 12. The combination of elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir DF can increase the levels of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Cobicistat, a CYP3A4 inhibitor, is contraindicated with CYP3A4 substrates that have elevated plasma concentrations associated with serious or life-threatening events. 13. Encorafenib may increase the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting BCRP transporters. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Encorafenib, as a BCRP inhibitor, may increase the concentration and toxicities of BCRP substrates. Close monitoring for signs of increased exposure and dose adjustments of these substrates are recommended. 14. Erythromycin base may decrease the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. Antibiotics may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. 15. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate may reduce the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are recommended. Antibiotics may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. 16. Erythromycin lactobionate may decrease the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. Antibiotics may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. 17. Erythromycin stearate may reduce the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are recommended. Antibiotics may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. 18. Etravirine may decrease the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. The efficacy of hormonal contraceptives may be reduced, and the use of a non-hormonal contraceptive method is recommended. 19. Ethinylestradiol may reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetic medications, such as exenatide, by impairing glucose tolerance. Patients should be advised to take oral contraceptives at least one hour before exenatide administration.
